entities.title: VPN control covers only scutil-managed VPNs
entities.summary: Only VPNs listed by scutil --nc (built-in IKEv2/IPSec/L2TP and Network-Extension VPNs such as WireGuard) are read and reconnected; other clients, including Cisco Secure Client/AnyConnect, are only observed through their tunnel routes.
entities.impact: A tunnel from another client is reported as UNSUPPORTED with its state unreadable, and a fault in it gets manual advice instead of a reconnect. --vpn cannot sign in when MFA or SSO is required.
entities.workaround: Reconnect the client yourself, from its own app or the menu bar.

relationships.description: Control of Cisco Secure Client/AnyConnect is deferred work.

entities.title: Tested against a scripted Mac, not a real one
entities.summary: The scripted command output the tests use follows documented macOS formats; it was not captured from a real Mac, and the repair steps have not yet run on one.
entities.impact: A difference between the documented formats and what a real Mac prints, or a repair step that behaves differently on real hardware, would not be caught by the tests.
entities.details: Every command, lookup and connection goes through the Sys trait, and the tests drive the whole tool against sys::fake::Fake; see verification.json.
entities.origin: Moved from the second bullet of Limitations in macos/rust/fix-network/README.md.

entities.title: Wi-Fi association is judged by the address, not the SSID
entities.summary: The tool never asks which network the Mac joined; a Wi-Fi link counts as up when it has a usable IPv4 or global IPv6 address.
entities.impact: Being joined to the wrong network is not reported as such.

entities.title: macOS only
entities.summary: On any other OS every command is refused with exit status 2 before anything runs.
entities.impact: The binary builds and its tests run on Linux, but it cannot diagnose a Linux machine.

entities.title: What the tool never does
entities.summary: No reboot, no router changes, no deleting network preferences, VPN profiles or keychains, no public DNS in place of the configured servers, no edits to scoped DNS or MDM-managed settings, no killing VPN processes, no stored credentials.
entities.impact: Problems that need one of these end as 'not fixable by this tool' or 'reboot needed', and the person does it.
entities.details: The repair steps are exactly the eight in model.rs's Step; none of them does any of the above. The DNS-server finding says that public DNS is never substituted automatically.

entities.title: Proxy repair disables only web and secure web proxies on the active service
entities.summary: --fix-proxy turns off an unreachable HTTP or HTTPS proxy on the service in use; an unreachable PAC file is reported but never changed.
entities.impact: A proxy set by a managed profile or on another service is left as it is, and the step fails with that explanation.
